parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module holds one concern: order and stock use cases, plus the DTO mapping they share. Every use case reaches persistence only through the domain ports it receives in its constructor (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockReservationService, IdGenerator). No file uses a database, ORM or query client directly. DTO mapping is defined once in dtos.ts (toOrderDto, toStockLevelDto) and every use case calls those functions rather than copying them. ListOrdersByStateUseCase calls the domain's shared assertOrderState instead of re-implementing the state check, so the module uses its abstractions consistently. Three use cases repeat the same lookup guard: `findById` followed by `throw NotFoundError`. That is a short way of handling a missing order, not a copied business rule or invariant, so I don't count it as a violation. PlaceOrderUseCase checks raw request input (customerId, items, productId) in the application layer. The source shows no second copy of those checks inside this unit.
